latest_news.headline: Explosive drone incident raises NATO-logistics concern; attribution remains unestablished
latest_news.text: Reuters reported German federal prosecutors are investigating an explosive-laden drone found at Leipzig/Halle airport, a major civilian cargo and NATO logistics hub. A second suspected drone struck a DHL aircraft with slight damage. Authorities had not established the drone origin or attribution; Russia called accusations a fabricated provocation. This is a high-priority watch item, not evidence for a configured russia signal.

latest_news.headline: Taiwan reports no abnormal activity under PRC traffic-control order during Typhoon Hana
latest_news.text: Reuters reported Taiwan said a PRC traffic-control order off Fujian was issued as Typhoon Hana approached. Taiwan's defence ministry reported no abnormal ship or aircraft activity; weather attribution means no new military_buildup signal is activated.

latest_news.headline: UN Security Council extends Red Sea attack reporting as members condemn recent Houthi strikes
latest_news.text: UN meeting coverage says the Security Council adopted Resolution 2826 by 13-0-2, extending monthly reporting on Houthi Red Sea attacks through January 15, 2027. Several members cited recent Houthi strikes against Saudi Arabia and freedom-of-navigation risks. Existing ceasefire_violation remains active; no separate probability increment is applied.
sources: United Nations Security Council meeting coverage

latest_news.headline: Houthis strike Marib again; UN warns Yemen is nearing wider conflict
latest_news.text: Reuters reported ballistic missiles and drones hit displacement camps and residential neighbourhoods in Marib, killing two and wounding 14 according to local authorities. The attack followed strikes that killed at least 30 government troops. The UN envoy called this the highest risk of renewed large-scale conflict since the 2022 truce. The existing ceasefire_violation indicator is renewed; risk holds 85 because the lane already absorbed the escalation and no distinct infrastructure strike or verified buildup was established.

latest_news.headline: U.S. official expects Hormuz deal soon, but traffic remains severely depressed
latest_news.text: Reuters reported a U.S. official expects an Iran-Oman agreement that could restore normal shipping, while Kpler counted just 33 Hormuz transits Monday-Thursday versus 50 a week earlier and four on Thursday. The diplomatic channel is material but remains unsigned and unimplemented; existing diplomacy_active and hormuz_controlled_not_closed indicators remain active with no probability change.

latest_news.headline: Taiwan continues scheduled Han Kuang coastal-strike and continuity drills
latest_news.text: Reuters reported President Lai overseeing coastal-strike training during Taiwan’s annual war games. The exercise is defensive and scheduled; no fresh PLA blockade, Chinese live-fire action or armed clash was verified, so China remains 24 raw / 29 coupled with no canonical signal change.

latest_news.headline: Lebanon and Israel agree shortlist for possible disarmament-verification force
latest_news.text: Reuters reported that the parties agreed a shortlist of countries that could send troops to verify a future Hezbollah-disarmament arrangement. Later reporting described positive movement on borders and prisoners. This reinforces diplomacy_active but does not offset continuing truce violations or justify a probability cut.

latest_news.headline: U.S. intelligence reportedly widens window for a possible Russian test of NATO
latest_news.text: The Wall Street Journal, citing new U.S. intelligence assessments, reported scenarios from hybrid attacks to a limited eastern-flank incursion between autumn 2026 and 2029; reporting says a ground incursion remains the least likely case. Lithuania also warned of possible false-flag drone attacks on Baltic infrastructure. No attack or NATO Article 4/5 action was verified, so the Russia tracker holds 70 raw / 80 coupled with no new canonical signal.
sources: Wall Street Journal via Kyiv Independent
Lithuanian defence minister via LRT/Kyiv Independent

latest_news.title: ADNOC says 15 of its vessels have been attacked since war began; three this week
latest_news.summary: ADNOC said missiles or drones have targeted 15 company vessels transiting Hormuz since the conflict began, including three this week; one crew member was killed and 20 injured. The disclosure materially reinforces the scale of shipping risk, but Iran conventional remains unchanged at its 95 raw ceiling with existing hormuz_controlled_not_closed, hormuz_mining and oil_infrastructure_threat signals already active.
latest_news.sources: ADNOC statement via Gulf News; Bloomberg; OilPrice

latest_news.headline: Congo completes first known prisoner transfer to AFC/M23 under Qatar deal
latest_news.text: Reuters and the ICRC said Congolese authorities released 15 prisoners to AFC/M23. The handover is one of the first concrete implementation steps under last year's Qatar agreement; it reinforces the existing diplomacy_active signal but does not resolve the wider conflict.
sources: International Committee of the Red Cross

latest_news.headline: African rights alliance seeks inquiry into Sudan chemical-weapons allegations
latest_news.text: The Sudan Coalition called for an independent inquiry into older allegations of chemical-weapons use by Sudan's army. No fresh attack was independently verified, so the item is retained as accountability context rather than a new configured scoring signal.

latest_news.headline: Houthi attacks kill scores in Yemen and wound 11 civilians in Saudi Arabia
latest_news.text: AFP reported 61 Yemeni government troops killed in ballistic-missile and drone attacks across Thursday-Friday, the worst losses since 2022. Saudi authorities separately said Houthi shelling in Najran wounded 11 civilians, including a four-year-old child; Yemen’s defence ministry promised a response. The EU and Canada subsequently condemned the attacks on Najran and Marib and called for an immediate halt; this is an allied-position update, not a new attack or an additional scoring input.

latest_news.headline: Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan formalize mutual-defence pact
latest_news.text: Reuters, AP and the signatories confirm that an armed attack on one member is to be regarded as an attack on all three. The public text does not specify nuclear sharing; the pact is tracked as an allied-position change, not a new Türkiye scoring signal.

latest_news.headline: Hormuz traffic falls to eight ships as proposed framework remains incomplete
latest_news.text: Kpler counted eight ships transiting Hormuz on Thursday, down from 13 per day the prior week and more than 100 daily before the war. Iran-Oman talks remain active, but a framework would not automatically reopen the strait and shipping sources question its operational feasibility.

latest_news.headline: Saudi Arabia warns of imminent coordinated attacks from north and south
latest_news.text: A senior Saudi official told Reuters that Saudi, US and regional intelligence indicated Houthis and Iraqi militias under IRGC supervision could target energy infrastructure, ports and airports; Riyadh said contacts and mediation were still moving in the right direction.

latest_news.headline: Lebanese soldier lightly injured by Israeli drone sound bomb after talks
latest_news.text: Lebanon’s army said an Israeli drone dropped a sound bomb on an army bulldozer clearing roads in Mansouri, lightly injuring a soldier. The incident followed the seventh round of US-brokered implementation talks on Thursday.

latest_news.headline: Iraq keeps forces on high alert after militia retaliation deadline
latest_news.text: Iraq raised readiness nationwide and reported exercises and troop movements as a militia retaliation deadline expired. Badr leader Hadi al-Ameri urged factions to postpone action, but disarmament resistance and regional strike warnings persist.
sources: Iraq Security Media Cell via The National

latest_news.headline: UNIFIL records sharpest Israel-Lebanon escalation since June framework
latest_news.text: UNIFIL recorded 113 Israeli projectiles on Aug. 5 and 120 more by late Aug. 6, plus airspace violations and strikes near Al Mansuri; it reported no Hezbollah launches during the same Aug. 5 period.
